newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK's Patten says Europe can learn from Asia. [CORRECTED 10:55 GMT]
newsitem.headline: HK's Patten says Europe can learn from Asia. [CORRECTED 10:55 GMT]

text.p: Hong Kong Governor Chris Patten told the annual World Economic Forum's Europe-East Asia summit on on Tuesday that Europe could learn from Asia.
In his opening address, Patten praised the virtues of low public expenditure, low taxes and the spirit of free market economics.
"Hong Kong has been blessed by a succession of financial secretaries spiritually, if not genetically, descended from Adam Smith," he said.
He was referring to the 19th century economist who advocated laissez-faire economics and the benefits of allowing the invisible hand of market forces free rein.
Hong Kong keeps public expenditure below 20 percent of Gross Domestic Product, Patten said, and is able to maintain a low tax regime allowing entrepreneurialism and wealth creation to flourish.
Only 40 percent of Hong Kong's working population pay salaries tax and only two percent pay the top rate of 15 percent (corrects tax rate), he said.

"I do not myself see how Europe is going to be able to reduce its prodigious and depressing levels of unemployment, especially among the young, without deregulating markets and reducing the social costs of employing people," he said.

The World Economic Forum programme for the day focuses on whether the East Asian economic dymamo is slowing or merely pausing, how European companies can compete successfully in Asian markets and cross-cultural challenges.
